definition: Innovate means to introduce new methods, ideas, or ways of doing something, especially within an existing field or process.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word innovate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know innovate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Rather than accept the confusing shift changes, the head nurse decided to innovate, introducing a bedside handoff method that cut medication errors in half.
To tinker is to make small trial-and-error adjustments, while to innovate is to introduce genuinely new methods or ideas into how something is done.
To innovate is to improve how something is done, but to revolutionize is to change a whole field so completely that the old ways disappear.

To modernize is to bring something up to date with the methods and technology already current, closing the gap with the present. To innovate is to introduce genuinely new methods or ideas, which may put you ahead of the current standard rather than merely level with it.

To pioneer is to be among the very first anywhere to open up a new method or field, and the word crowns whoever got there first. To innovate is to bring new methods or ideas into how something is done, whether or not you are first in the world.

To transform something is to change it so markedly that it looks or works like a different thing; the word measures the size of the change. To innovate names the act of introducing new methods or ideas, whether the change they bring is sweeping or modest.

Innovate means to introduce new methods, ideas, or ways of doing something, especially within an existing field or process.
Water bills were draining the vineyard's budget, so Elena chose to innovate: she introduced a scheduling method that watered each row only when its soil sensors reported real thirst.
The vines stayed just as healthy while water use fell by a third.
Elena does not build a brand-new machine; she introduces a new method for doing something the vineyard already did, and improving how an existing process works is exactly what it means to innovate.

Nobody expected the region's oldest hardware store to be its most inventive business.
Yet while chain rivals matched each other's current layouts and scanners, the Barlow brothers kept trying things nobody around them was doing.
They lent tools by the hour, printed replacement parts at a counter in the back, and taught free repair classes on Saturdays.
Trade papers called it a willingness to innovate inside a business most people considered finished.
None of it required being first in the world -- a tool library existed somewhere, surely -- but each idea was new to the trade in their valley, and it kept the doors open.
